newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmakers reject 'No Budget, No Pay' bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmakers reject 'No Budget, No Pay' bill.

text.p: California legislators on Monday rejected a bill that would dock the pay of lawmakers whenever they are late enacting the state budget.
The measure, by Republican Assemblyman Jim Morrissey, narrowly failed passage in the Assembly Budget Committee, state officials said.
Morrissey said his proposal would have provided a strong incentive to lawmakers to finalize the state's budget on time.
"We just need something to motivate people to do the job," the assemblyman said.

The legislature is required to approve the state budget no later than June 15, and it must be signed by the governor no later than June 30. But the governor and the legislature have routinely failed to meet the deadlines.
This year has been no different. Lawmakers have yet to approve the state's budget for the 1997-1998 fiscal year.
